coverage: Whole group totals · single retail segment · Star (Trent Hypermarket) included only as a share of loss
definition: Profit after tax that belongs to Trent’s own shareholders, after removing the small share earned by outside partners in Booker India (non-controlling interest). It includes Trent’s share of results from joint ventures and associates and is after a one-off Labour Codes charge. It is not store operating profit or cash.
sourceLabel: Integrated Annual Report 2025–26 · audited consolidated financial statements, as filed with BSE and NSE on 30 May 2026
location: PDF page 214 / printed page 331 · consolidated statement of profit and loss; PDF page 229 / printed page 361 · note 28, revenue; PDF page 230 / printed page 363 · note 33, exceptional items; PDF page 232 / printed page 367 · note 38, segment; PDF page 244 / printed page 391 · note 47, share of joint ventures and associates
notes: Revenue is revenue from operations: store and online sales net of GST, plus ₹224.10 crore of other operating income; it excludes ₹114.84 crore other income. Total group profit after tax was ₹1,721.33 crore, of which ₹1.68 crore belongs to outside partners in Booker. Profit is after a one-off ₹26.11 crore charge for the new Labour Codes. Star stores (Trent Hypermarket joint venture) are not in revenue; Trent’s share of their loss was ₹64.88 crore, partly offset by ₹70.40 crore from its associates Inditex Trent Retail India and Massimo Dutti India. Trent reports a single segment, so no profit is given for Westside, Zudio or other brands.
insight: Revenue grew about 17% compared with the previous year, while owners’ profit grew about 11%. Depreciation, the yearly cost of wear on stores and fittings, rose from ₹895 crore to ₹1,361 crore as the store count grew.
